incumbent.name: Sue Errington
incumbent.summary: Sue Errington, a Muncie Democrat, served in the state Senate from 2006 and has represented House District 34 since 2012; she announced in December 2025 that she would not seek reelection {ihdc_errington} {ipr_errington}. She is the ranking minority member of the Environmental Affairs Committee {ihdc_errington}.
record: Committees: ranking minority member, Environmental Affairs; member, Elections and Apportionment; vice chair, Statutory Committee on Ethics, according to the House Democratic caucus {ihdc_errington}.

2025 session: Authored HEA 1297, which created Indiana's Yellow Dot Program to give first responders quick access to medical information; the House honored her service with House Resolution 24 on Feb. 10, 2026 {ihdc_honored}.
2025: Voted no on SEA 1, the property-tax law (passed House 65-29) {rc_sea1_433}, and on the 2025 budget conference report (adopted 66-27) {rc_hb1001_576}.
Dec. 2025: Offered an amendment to HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill, that failed 27-67 {rc_hb1032_11}, then voted no on the bill, which passed the House 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}.

race_context: House District 34 covers part of Delaware County, including most of Muncie {wfyi_guide34} {sp_2024}.
Open seat: Errington is retiring after 14 years in the House {ipr_errington}. IPR reports Democrats have held the seat nearly continuously for decades {ipr_primary}.

May 5, 2026 primaries: Richard Ivy won the Republican nomination with 53.22% over Randall McCallister {ipr_primary} {wlbc_primary}; Sara Gullion was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {wlbc_primary}. Two other Republicans, Chris Walker and Tim Overton, withdrew in February {wb_withdraw}.
The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee lists the seat among its target races {dlcc_gullion}.

Key differences: Gullion lists raising the minimum wage, a moratorium on new data centers and restoring abortion access among her priorities {gullion_issues}; Ivy lists infrastructure, public safety, economic development and fiscal prudence {ivy_site} {sp_ivy}. No detailed statements from Ivy on data centers, property taxes or wages were found.

No general-election debate or forum for this race was found. Muncie Resists invited state legislative primary candidates to a March 19, 2026 forum in Muncie {mj_forums}; which candidates attended was not reported.

candidates.summary: Sara Gullion is a Muncie City Council member and paralegal running as a Democrat with Errington's endorsement {ipr_errington} {wfyi_guide34}. She lists housing affordability, fair wages, accessible health care and public schools as priorities {gullion_about}.
background: Member of the Muncie City Council, where she says she has "championed accountability, transparency and fairness" over the past two years {gullion_about} {ipr_errington}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wlbc_primary} {ipr_primary}.

items: Would raise the minimum wage, index it to inflation and raise the subminimum wage for tipped workers {gullion_issues}.
Supports more state investment in affordable housing and stronger renter protections and eviction prevention {gullion_issues}.
Supports pre-K for all and ensuring "Hoosiers' taxes go toward public schools" {gullion_issues}; calls child care infrastructure {gullion_issues}.
Supports a moratorium on more data centers, with public hearings, environmental impact assessments and limits tied to local capacity before permits are approved {gullion_issues}.
Supports restoring abortion access, expanding mental health care access, and LGBTQ+ nondiscrimination protections {gullion_issues}.

on_incumbent: Says Errington encouraged her to run and that she would remind state decision-makers "that their votes affect real people with real needs, who deserve real affordability" {gullion_about}. No statements about Ivy were found.
plans: Says she will continue to advocate for and respond to constituents and bring a local-government perspective to the Statehouse {gullion_about}.
endorsements_finance: Endorsed by Rep. Sue Errington, who IPR reported would run her campaign {ipr_errington}.
Listed as a target race by the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee {dlcc_gullion}.
Top donors listed by WFYI via Transparency USA include Indiana Conservation Voters and Carey Hamilton {wfyi_guide34}.
gaps: Did not answer WFYI's survey; positions come from her campaign website.
Her campaign's endorsements page was empty when checked.
Muncie City Council district and votes not reviewed; age not verified.

candidates.summary: Richard Ivy is human resources director for the Muncie Sanitary District and a former Muncie deputy mayor, running as a Republican {wfyi_guide34} {sp_ivy}. He lists infrastructure, public safety, economic development and opportunities for youth, seniors and working families as priorities {ivy_site}.
background: Human resources director, Muncie Sanitary District; lives in Muncie {wfyi_guide34} {ivy_site}.

Former Muncie deputy mayor; the Star Press reported the city council eliminated funding for that position in 2024 {sp_ivy}. As deputy mayor he oversaw departments including public works, parks and public safety, according to his campaign release {sp_ivy}.
Previously worked at LifeStream Services, serving seniors and people with disabilities, per his campaign release; finance secretary at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church {sp_ivy}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 53.22% over Randall McCallister {ipr_primary} {wlbc_primary}.

items: Says his deputy mayor experience taught him how to get state money "funneled down to Muncie" and that constituents want "expansion, jobs, and lack of increasing taxes" {ipr_primary}.
Lists public safety and neighborhood revitalization among priorities {ivy_site} {sp_ivy}.
Lists transparency, restoring public trust, and "fiscal prudence and data-informed decision making" as priorities {sp_ivy}.

on_incumbent: After winning the primary, Ivy said, "I think it's our time and our place to win this seat back and bring value back to Muncie through the state representation" {ipr_primary}.
On Gullion: "Me and her have no difficulty getting along in the past. So, I think it'll be a clean race" {ipr_primary}.
plans: Says he would support seniors, veterans and families and expand youth opportunities and workforce pathways {sp_ivy}.
endorsements_finance: Top donors listed by WFYI via Transparency USA include five individuals {wfyi_guide34}.
gaps: Did not answer WFYI's survey; no detailed positions on property taxes, data centers, education or redistricting found.
IPR said Ivy cited city council experience; his council service was not confirmed.
No endorsements or fundraising totals found.
